ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: judging armour and clothes
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: One number from 1 to 10 for every piece of armour and clothing, where it protects, how warm it keeps a colonist in your weather, and how it suits each colonist
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A parka isn't marked down for stopping no bullets, nor marine armour for its weight: each piece is judged against its own kind, body armour against body armour, a hat against hats.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Every piece a colonist can wear, from the game, its DLCs and your mods, has a rating from 1.0 to 10.0 at the top of its info card, worked out from what it really does for its wearer by the game's own rules. Beside it: sub-ratings, colour-coded tags with the reason for each, a line in plain words, and its effects, counted or only named. Rimfolk's apparel card shows where it protects, how warm it keeps a colonist in your weather, and how it compares with what they wear.

points.li: A colonist of Shooting 8 and Melee 8 with no traits wears the piece alone, with an assault rifle or a steel longsword, against what a colony meets after its first year: raiders' guns and grenades, their blades and fists, animals, mechanoids and fire.

Armour by the game's own roll, on the parts it covers: a shot can land on any part, a blow or a blast only on an outer one, a hit on the head counts twice. Each hit rolls the armour less its piercing: up to half of it turns the hit away, the rest halves the damage, and a sharp hit halved goes on as blunt. Armour is held at 200%.

What it costs and adds: a slower walk, worse aim or melee, work and talks, the mind, psycasts, a mechanitor's bandwidth, toxins and vacuum, carrying and hunting; shields, jumps, smoke, low shields, firefoam and what it throws or calls. What a mod's own code does is valued where its code was read, and otherwise named and marked rough.

Each piece is judged against its own kind: body armour, helmets, shields for the off hand, belts and packs, cold- and hot-weather gear, hazard suits, everyday clothing, hats, ceremonial and psychic pieces. 5.5 is the middle of each.

Every piece is rated for a shooter and for a melee fighter. One that clearly suits one of them, a shield belt that stops its wearer's own shots, a jump pack that carries a melee fighter onto the enemy, is rated for that one, and both ratings show where they differ by half a point.
Its own quality and material change its rating, by the game's own stats: a legendary parka keeps warmer and turns more, an awful one less, a devilstrand duster more than a cloth one.

Wear doesn't weaken armour in the game, but its wearer minds it: below half its hit points, and more so below a fifth, a colonist is unhappy wearing it, and that mood counts against it. Clothes taken from the dead count their mood the same way. Every hit that reaches a piece wears it by a quarter of the hit's damage.
A piece biocoded to someone names them; the rating doesn't change.

li.heading: Tags
li.text: Each piece shows its most telling tags, seven at most, each given by a rule on its own numbers with the reason on its tooltip, in the weapons' six kinds and colours: strengths (green, up), weaknesses (red, down), risks (orange, a warning), specials (violet, a star), roles (blue, a diamond) and what it needs (grey, a dot).

points.li: The piece's own picture, large, framed in the colour of its quality, the badge, the tags as chips, the line in plain words and the sub-ratings.

Protection by body part: a figure of the body filled where it covers, each region with its share of the shots that hit a colonist and how much of it the piece covers, and its sharp, blunt and heat armour.

Warmth against the weather: the temperature outside now and the season's range on the colonist's map, from its nights to its days, against the range the piece keeps them comfortable in with what else they wear, and whether that holds through the season.

The piece as it is: its quality and material, its hit points with the game's two marks for the mood of worn clothes, how many days of wear to the first, whether it was taken from the dead, whom it is biocoded to.
Its rating in other materials, the situations it suits, every effect and the key numbers.

With "Open Rimfolk's apparel card first" (on at first), opening the info for a piece anywhere opens this card instead of the game's. Its button "All the game's stats" opens the game's own card for the same piece, and the game's card keeps its button back. Links followed inside the game's card stay in it. A piece's kind (from the research or architect tab, or a list) is rated as made: normal quality, in its usual material (devilstrand for fabric, steel for metal), and its card says so.
The card rates the piece for the colonist who wears or carries it, or one you choose, step by step from the usual rating, each step named with how much it moves it.

How they fight: a gun in hand makes them a shooter, a blade a melee fighter; with neither, a brawler fights in melee, and their skills decide when four levels apart. Someone incapable of violence is rated only on how long they last.
Their body: what it covers counts on the body they have, so a part they lost no longer counts.

Their weather: warmth and cooling count by what the season asks of this piece beyond what they keep wearing. The degrees it asks count in full, those beyond at a fifth, so a second warm coat is worth little to someone dressed for the cold.
Moods it would add: made for the other gender, or worn when their other clothes are already as worn, which adds nothing.
What it would take the place of: what they wear now on the same layer over the same parts, each rated for them, and the difference.

li.heading: On the gear tab
li.text: A small badge with the rating beside each piece a colonist wears or carries, on the game's gear tab and on Nice Inventory Tab's rows, apparel slots and inventory, its tooltip the tags and the colonist's own rating ("Ratings on the gear tab", on). A click on it opens Rimfolk's apparel card.
